text:
mike-customer: Hi, after pulling the latest tagged release of our Go SDK (v2.0.0) clients started failing in CI with `module declares its path` and runtime panics. This started ~3pm PST yesterday.
sara-support: sorry to hear that, could you paste the exact error from CI and your go.mod?
mike-customer: CI log snippet:
```
go: github.com/redwood/sdk v2.0.0: reading github.com/redwood/sdk/go.mod: 403 Forbidden
go: error loading module requirements
```
And our go.mod contains:
```
module github.com/acme/service
require github.com/redwood/sdk v2.0.0
replace github.com/redwood/sdk => github.com/redwood/sdk v2.0.0
```
sara-support: odd to `replace` to the same path+version. can you also `git ls-remote --tags` output for that repo?
mike-customer: `git ls-remote --tags git@github.com:redwood/sdk.git` shows the tag v2.0.0 but its commit hash doesn't match what we pulled earlier. Might have been force-pushed.
ash-eng: tagging force-push would explain both the 403 and checksum issues if GOPROXY/cache had the old object. @ash-eng tagging history looks suspicious.
ash-eng: deploy-bot reports a release publish event at 2025-08-12T22:10Z: `release/v2.0.0 created` then `release/v2.0.0 force-updated`.
sara-support: ok escalation path: can you reproduce locally with `GOPROXY=direct GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood go get -v github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.0` and paste output?
mike-customer: running that gives:
```
go get github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.0: verifying module: github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.0: reading https://sum.golang.org/lookup/github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.0: remote error: checksum mismatch
```
noah-ops: checksum mismatch + force-push = sumdb rejecting the new tag. If a tag was re-pointed CI and consumers who cached the old checksum will fail.
sara-support: thanks, we'll escalate to eng infra. @ash-eng can you confirm if a tag was recreated? If so, what's the mitigation?
ash-eng: confirmed: there was an accidental force-push that moved v2.0.0 to a different commit. We patched the repo but the old tag is gone from git history in a couple mirrors.
ash-eng: mitigation options:
- recreate the original tag pointing to the original commit (if we still have the SHA in backups) and push it (preferred).
- bump to v2.0.1 and publish a clean release, update SDK consumers to v2.0.1.
- advise customers to pin a specific commit pseudo-version (not ideal).
sara-support: for customers blocked in CI we should provide a short repro workaround: `go clean -modcache && GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/redwood/sdk@<commit>` or `require github.com/redwood/sdk v0.0.0-<commit>` in go.mod. Also recommend `git fetch --tags --force` if they control the remote.
mike-customer: is there risk of runtime panics if we switch to the new commit/tag? They mentioned interface shape changed between commits.
ash-eng: yes, API surface changed across commits — that's why the panic. If you must keep compatibility, pin to the commit that matches your built code.
ash-eng: long-term fix: we will republish v2.0.1 with the intended code and coordinate a migration note. We'll also open INC-11987 and notify customers in status.
sara-support: created INC-11987 and a customer-facing note draft: "We experienced an accidental force-push that affected tagged release v2.0.0 of the Go SDK. If you see checksum or tag-not-found errors, upgrade to v2.0.1 or pin to the commit SHA while we restore tags." cc @noah-ops
noah-ops: I'm going to clear the internal mirror cache and add a GHE tag mirror job to preserve tags for 30 days. Also adding a policy: forbid force pushes on `refs/tags/*`.
mike-customer: thanks — can you tell me the replacement tag name or commit to pin to?
ash-eng: publishing v2.0.1 now (pushed tag at 2025-08-13T02:05Z). New tag points to commit `abc123def456`. Use `go get github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.1` or `require github.com/redwood/sdk v2.0.1` in go.mod.
sara-support: quick checklist we sent to the customer:
- try `go clean -modcache`
- `GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/redwood/sdk@v2.0.1`
- if still failing, add `GONOSUMDB=github.com/redwood` or pin to SHA: `require github.com/redwood/sdk v0.0.0-20250813020500-abc123def456`
- as last resort, vendor the module.
mike-customer: `go get v2.0.1` fixed CI, but we had to update one call site due to a breaking change noted in the changelog. all good now. thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
sara-support: great, closing the customer ticket after follow-up. we'll publish the postmortem and the policy change to eng channel.
ash-eng: one more internal action: add an automated check during release to fail if `git push --tags --force` is attempted and require a release-approve step.
ash-eng: filing a follow-up to add tag immutability checks to our release automation.
deploy-bot: [release] v2.0.1 published for github.com/redwood/sdk at abc123def456
noah-ops: notifying infra team to review artifact retention and sumdb mirrors.
sara-support: thanks everyone, marking resolved for this thread.
